headline: Two hurdles world records fall on the same night in Zurich
dek: Alison dos Santos ran 45.80 over 400m and Masai Russell 12.09 over 100m at Weltklasse Zürich. Both marks still have to be ratified by World Athletics.
summary: Brazil's Alison dos Santos broke the 400m hurdles world record with 45.80 and Masai Russell took the 100m hurdles record with 12.09 at Weltklasse Zürich on 27 August; both await ratification.

body.text: Two world records went in the space of one evening at the Letzigrund stadium in Zurich on Thursday 27 August. Alison dos Santos of Brazil won the men's 400m hurdles in 45.80, and Masai Russell of the United States won the women's 100m hurdles in 12.09. World Athletics and the Wanda Diamond League both reported the marks; neither is official until the sport's governing body completes ratification.

Dos Santos took 0.14 off a record that had stood for five years. The previous mark, 45.94, was set by Norway's Karsten Warholm in the Olympic final in Tokyo in 2021. Warholm was in the Zurich field and finished second in 46.69. Ezekiel Nathaniel of Nigeria was third in 47.50.

Speaking afterwards in comments carried by the Diamond League, dos Santos credited his coach, saying he had made the run possible and had believed in him when he was younger. He also said he hoped Brazil had stopped to watch.
The crowd and the energy were perfect. This night was amazing for me and for everyone who came to watch.
body.cite: Alison dos Santos, via World Athletics and the Wanda Diamond League

body.text: Russell's 12.09 improved the record by 0.03. The previous mark of 12.12 belonged to Tobi Amusan of Nigeria, who was in the Zurich race and finished second in 12.23. Nadine Visser of the Netherlands was third in 12.34.
When I saw 12.09, I got so emotional. I have dreamed about this moment for so long.

The two records were not the only marks of the night. Audrey Werro of Switzerland won the women's 800m at home in 1:53.70, which FloTrack recorded as a Swiss national record, a Diamond League record and the fastest time in the world this year. Julien Alfred of Saint Lucia won the women's 100m in 10.70, a national record, from Melissa Jefferson-Wooden of the United States, also timed at 10.70. Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage of Sri Lanka won the javelin with 92.07m, and Miltiadis Tentoglou of Greece the long jump with 8.45m.

A world record is not a world record on the night. World Athletics requires the performance to pass a set of checks before it enters the books — among them the validity of the timing equipment, wind readings within the legal limit for the event, and a doping control test taken at the meeting. The process is routine for a well-run Diamond League meeting and rarely overturns a mark, but it is not finished, and both times are best described as pending until it is.

World Athletics described Zurich as the last regular-season meeting of the Diamond League before the final, which it said would be held in Brussels a week later. The wider context, for both athletes, is a season that ends there.

items: Men's 400m hurdles: Alison dos Santos (Brazil) 45.80 — previous record 45.94, Karsten Warholm, Tokyo 2021
Women's 100m hurdles: Masai Russell (United States) 12.09 — previous record 12.12, Tobi Amusan
Both subject to ratification by World Athletics

uncertain: Neither time is an official world record until World Athletics completes ratification.

Sources date the meeting slightly differently: World Athletics and the Diamond League place the record night on 27 August, while FloTrack lists the meeting across 26–27 August. Weltklasse Zürich has in past years held some field events in the city centre the evening before the main programme, which may account for the difference.
The detail that the Diamond League final follows in Brussels a week later comes from World Athletics' report; the final's schedule was not separately checked for this article.
The supporting results are as recorded by FloTrack and were not cross-checked line by line against the official results service.
